question: Do the disc rows of oadec verify agree with the stream validity table Dolby's TrueHD encoder prints, pass the Blu-ray streams of the corpus, and say no where their sources do?

sources.blu_ray: BDA, White Paper BD-ROM Audio Visual Application Format Specifications, version 2.5 (2011), Figure 3-4: Dolby Lossless at 48, 96 and 192 kHz, eight channels at 48 and 96 kHz and six at 192 kHz, 18.64 Mbit/s, 16 to 24 bits
sources.syntax: Dolby TrueHD (MLP) High-Level Bitstream Description (2018), section 1: the FBA syntax is the one Blu-ray uses, the FBB syntax the one DVD-Audio uses
sources.hd_dvd: the verifier messages of Dolby's TrueHD encoder (dee_dthd_encoder, Dolby Encoding Engine 5.7.2), read as strings of the program and not decompiled: at high-resolution rates an FBA presentation may have at most two channels for HD DVD-Video and at most six for Blu-ray; no message bounds the rates HD DVD takes, while one refuses a sampling frequency for a stream made for Blu-ray

method: tools: oadec verify --json on (1) every encode of Dolby's TrueHD encoder kept from the buffer work, against the stream validity table of its verification report; (2) streams FFmpeg's TrueHD encoder wrote at the rates Dolby's encoder refuses (44.1 and 192 kHz input, 'Unsupported sample-rate'), 2.0 and 5.1, since FFmpeg writes at most six channels; (3) the real corpus of the earlier evidence: Blu-ray TrueHD streams, the encoder-written deliveries and three full damaged titles. The logs and streams are not committed.

dolby_encodes.note: every encode is 48 or 96 kHz FBA, so the table says yes, yes, no for each; the rows that say no for other reasons are judged on the streams below

ffmpeg_streams.what: FFmpeg's TrueHD encoder declares a peak data rate near 9.6 Mbit/s whatever it writes; at 96 and 192 kHz with six channels it delivers above it, and at 192 kHz above 18 Mbit/s, so its pink-noise 5.1 streams carry delivery findings and fail verify on the timing (exit 7). The tone at 192 kHz stays within its bounds.

reading: On 12 encodes of Dolby's encoder the rows match its validity table, 36 of 36. Where its encoder will not go, the rows follow their sources: a 5.1 stream at 192 kHz within its delivery bounds fits Blu-ray and not HD DVD; 44.1 and 176.4 kHz keep a stream off Blu-ray and leave HD DVD unjudged. 49 of the 51 corpus streams fit Blu-ray; the 2 that do not are the damaged titles, kept off by delivery findings that lie in their damage regions (365 and 121 findings, none outside a damage region); both checks are ones Dolby's encoder names in its verifier messages.
